2027-02-02.title: The Presentation of the Lord
readings: The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple
Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory
My eyes have seen your salvation, a light for revelation to the Gentiles
2027-02-02.alt: Feast. Blessing of candles and procession (or solemn entrance) before Mass. Gloria is said. World Day for Consecrated Life. Forty days after Christmas. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-02-02.verse: for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.”
theo: Malachi spoke to a tired people whose worship had grown careless, and promised: “See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.” But he warned: “who can endure the day of his coming… For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap.” Israel expected a king in glory. Today the promise is fulfilled in a way no one imagined: the Lord comes to his temple as a forty-day-old child, carried in his mother's arms, and the offering made for him is “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons”, the offering of the poor.

Mary and Joseph come to fulfil the law: every firstborn son belongs to the Lord and must be presented to him, and the mother offers the sacrifice of purification. They come as ordinary, obedient, poor people. Yet the Spirit is at work. Simeon, “righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel”, comes “guided by the Spirit” into the temple, takes the child in his arms, and sings: “Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace… for my eyes have seen your salvation… a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.” An old man holds the infant who holds the universe. The Church sings his song every night at Compline.

Then Simeon turns to Mary: “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed… and a sword will pierce your own soul too.” The light will be a light from the cross, and Mary will stand beneath it. Anna, a widow of eighty-four who “never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day”, speaks of the child to all who were waiting. Hebrews explains why he came so low: “he had to become like his brothers and sisters in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest.” Today the Church blesses candles, because Christ is the light, and celebrates all consecrated men and women who, like Anna, give their whole lives to God.
conn: Leviticus 12 prescribed the mother's purification forty days after the birth of a son; Exodus 13 required the consecration of every firstborn.
Leviticus 12:8 allows two turtledoves or two pigeons for those who cannot afford a lamb. Mary brings the offering of the poor, while carrying the true Lamb.
The Greek name of the feast means “the Meeting”: the Lord meets his people in Simeon and Anna.
Simeon's song (Luke 2:29–32) is prayed every night in the Church's Night Prayer.
From the fifth century in Jerusalem the feast was kept with lighted candles; candles blessed today are taken home for prayer, sickness and storms.
Since 1997 Pope St John Paul II made this day the World Day for Consecrated Life.
altar: The child presented in the temple is the same Lord offered on the altar. The temple of Jerusalem has become every church where the Mass is offered.
At Communion we, like Simeon, receive the Lord into our hands and hearts. Many priests pray the Nunc dimittis after Mass: now you dismiss your servant in peace.

Simeon longed to be released from the body as from a prison; having seen the Lord, he asks to depart in peace, for he who sees Christ need not fear death.
magis: The Presentation is a joint commemoration of the Son and the Mother: the offering of Christ and the faith of Mary.
Consecrated life as a total offering to God, a sign for the whole Church.

saints: Honoured in the Eastern Churches on 3 February as the God-receiver and the prophetess; models of patient, prayerful waiting.
2027-02-02.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, we humbly implore your majesty that, just as your Only Begotten Son was presented on this day in the Temple in the substance of our flesh, so, by your grace, we may be presented to you with minds made pure. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

catechism: The Presentation of Jesus in the temple.
kidsaint: Two old people who waited in the temple for many years to see God's promised Saviour. When Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus, they knew him at once and praised God. Lesson: if we pray and wait, God lets us see him!
2027-02-02.special: Feast of the Presentation of the Lord (Candlemas). World Day for Consecrated Life.
term: The traditional English name of today's feast, from the blessing of candles. The candles remind us that Christ is the light of the world.

family.explain: Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus to the temple. An old man named Simeon took him in his arms and thanked God, because he saw that this baby was the Saviour, the light for all people.
family.intention: We pray for all priests, sisters and brothers who have given their lives to God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family be a light for others this week?”

illus: In a convent in Kollam an old sister, nearly ninety, could no longer teach or nurse. Each morning she sat in the chapel with a small candle beside her and prayed for every name the other sisters brought her. A young novice asked whether she missed working. She smiled: I am Anna now. I never leave the temple. Someone must keep the light burning while the others go out.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you came to your temple in the arms of Mary. Come to us now and make us your light. Amen.
share: The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple (Malachi 3:1). Am I seeking him?
My eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:30). Where have I seen God's salvation?
A sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:35). What sorrow can I unite with Mary's?
pm.resp: Christ, light of the world, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may carry Christ's light to all nations.
For all consecrated men and women, on their world day.
For the elderly who wait in faith, like Simeon and Anna.
For our group, that we may offer our lives to God.
pm.close: Father, your Son was presented in the temple as the light of the nations. Purify our hearts and present us to you, burning with his light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, through the prophet Malachi God promised: the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple (Malachi 3:1). Israel expected a king in glory. Today the Lord comes to his temple as a little child, carried in his mother's arms.

Mary and Joseph come to fulfil the law. They bring the offering of the poor, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons (Luke 2:24). The one who will be the true Lamb is redeemed with the gift of the poor. God enters our world through humility and obedience.

Simeon, guided by the Spirit, takes the child in his arms and sings: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace… for my eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:29–30). An old man holds the One who holds the universe. That is why we carry candles today: Christ is a light for revelation to the Gentiles.

But Simeon also tells Mary: this child is destined for the falling and the rising of many… and a sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:34–35). The light will shine from the cross. Mary offers her Son today and will offer him again on Calvary.

Anna, a widow of eighty-four, never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2:37). Today we thank God for all consecrated men and women who, like Anna, give their whole lives to him.

Hebrews says he became like us in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest (Hebrews 2:17). Let us present ourselves to him today, and carry his light into every dark place. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary and Joseph took baby Jesus to God's house. Old Simeon held him and said: this baby is the light for the whole world!
When you see a candle in church, remember: Jesus is our light. Let us shine for him.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, who were the first people in the temple to recognise the Lord? Not the priests on duty, not the teachers of the law. Two old people: Simeon and Anna. Luke tells us that Simeon was righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit rested on him (Luke 2:25).

Simeon had received a promise: he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Messiah (Luke 2:26). Imagine the years of waiting. Every morning he went up to the temple; every evening he went home without seeing anything. But he did not give up. The prophet says: if it seems to tarry, wait for it; it will surely come, it will not delay (Habakkuk 2:3).

Then one day the Spirit led him into the temple at the very hour when a poor young couple walked in with their baby. Simeon took the child in his arms and praised God. The whole of his long waiting was gathered into one moment. He could now say: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace (Luke 2:29). A life spent waiting for God ends in peace.

And Anna, a widow of eighty-four, who never left the temple, came at that very moment, began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luke 2:38). She could not keep the good news to herself. Our grandparents were like this. Many of us received the faith from an old woman with a rosary who spoke of Jesus to anyone who would listen.

Today, as we carry our candles, let us thank God for the elderly in our families and parishes. Let us visit them, listen to them, and learn from them how to wait for the Lord. And when we come to the Mass, let us receive him as Simeon did, with joy and peace. Amen.

opts.a: The refiner's fire and the merciful high priest
intro: Malachi warns that the Lord who comes to his temple is like a refiner's fire. Hebrews tells us that the same Lord shares our flesh and blood. Today both truths meet in a little child.

points.apply: Make a good confession before the end of this month.

sub: The fear of death is broken.

homily: Dear friends, the prophet Malachi promised that the Lord would come to his temple. But then he asked a frightening question: who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap (Malachi 3:2).

A goldsmith puts gold into the fire not to destroy it but to burn away what is false. Malachi says the Lord will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, until they present offerings to the LORD in righteousness (Malachi 3:3). Every trial, every confession, every hard season can be God's fire purifying us. Peter writes that our faith is more precious than gold that is tested by fire (1 Peter 1:7).

And how does this fire come to the temple? As a baby forty days old, in his mother's arms. The Letter to the Hebrews explains: since, therefore, the children share flesh and blood, he himself likewise shared the same things, so that through death he might destroy the one who has the power of death (Hebrews 2:14). He comes close in our own flesh, so that his fire warms and does not burn us.

Hebrews continues: because he himself was tested by what he suffered, he is able to help those who are being tested (Hebrews 2:18). God once said to Moses: I have observed the misery of my people (Exodus 3:7). In Jesus he does more than observe: he enters our misery. There is no sorrow, no fear, no temptation that he does not understand from inside.

So let us not be afraid of the Lord who comes. Let us allow him to purify us in a good confession, and let us bring to him the trials that weigh on us. The candle we hold today burns and gives light at the same time. May our lives, purified by his fire, give light to others. Amen.
